methodComparison.imitationLearning: Learn actions from demonstrations; the LeRobot tutorial supplies a concrete collect/train/evaluate workflow.
methodComparison.reinforcementLearning: Learn a policy from interaction and reward; the Reacher project makes observation, action, reward, training and evaluation explicit.
methodComparison.policyBoundary: A policy produces actions. The saved jobs also demand the surrounding data, calibration, timing, control interface, evaluation and deployment work.
methodComparison.vlaBoundary: Vision-language-action models are one policy family within robot learning, not a universal prerequisite or distinct job title in this guide.

learningReferences.title: Spinning Up: Key Concepts in RL
learningReferences.supports: Policy maps observations/states to actions; RL learns through interaction to maximize cumulative reward; observation, action, trajectory and value terminology.
learningReferences.use: Conceptual foundation, not a claim that this older package is the preferred current installation.

learningReferences.title: Gymnasium Reacher
learningReferences.supports: Reacher-v5 is a two-joint arm with two continuous joint-torque actions, 10-element state observation, distance and action-effort reward, 50-step default horizon.
learningReferences.caution: Page has an internally inconsistent prose dt expression; avoid repeating it.

learningReferences.title: Stable Baselines3: RL Tips and Tricks
learningReferences.supports: Use quantitative experiments, multiple runs and a separate test environment; evaluate across episodes; check wrappers and time-limit handling. SAC handles continuous actions; PPO supports parallelized continuous-control training.
learningReferences.use: Evaluation method and bounded baseline choice.

learningReferences.title: MuJoCo Overview
learningReferences.supports: General-purpose articulated/contact physics engine, freely available and open source, with Python bindings and CPU simulation.
learningReferences.use: No robot purchase or simulator license fee required for the proposed simulated arm project; no runtime or cloud-cost promise.

learningReferences.title: Tobin et al., Domain Randomization for Transferring Deep Neural Networks from Simulation to the Real World (2017)
learningReferences.supports: Primary research example of randomized simulation appearance for real-world object localization and downstream grasping.
learningReferences.caution: The paper studies visual transfer; do not treat it as a guarantee of robust physical transfer for an unrelated policy.

learningReferences.title: LeRobot: Imitation Learning in Sim
learningReferences.supports: MuJoCo gym-hil demonstration recording, keyboard PandaPickCubeKeyboard-v0 option, LeRobotDataset, ACT training and simulated policy evaluation. Collection can use CPU/MPS; training example describes CUDA with MPS alternative.
learningReferences.caution: Main documentation requires source installation; runtime depends on compute, and tutorial mentions hours of training. Do not promise free cloud availability or quick laptop ACT training.

portfolioProposal.status: Proposed scoped learning artifact; no training run or performance result asserted.
portfolioProposal.primary: Gymnasium Reacher-v5 with state observations, a small policy and Stable Baselines3 SAC or PPO; start with random-policy baseline, document reward and action limits, then train under a declared time/compute budget.
portfolioProposal.evaluation: Separate train/evaluation seeds and target positions; multiple training seeds; episode return plus fingertip-to-target distance and a declared distance threshold for success. Threshold is project-defined, not a built-in industry metric. Keep reward/wrapper settings fixed for baseline comparison.
portfolioProposal.experiment: Compare original dynamics to one documented change in actuator strength or link mass using a custom MuJoCo XML model; report where return and goal error degrade. An optional next ablation trains with randomized parameters and retests the same held-out variants.
deliverables: Saved checkpoint, training budget and learning curves
Evaluation table across seeds/conditions with baseline
Failure notes connecting changed dynamics to observed errors
portfolioProposal.limits: No hardware purchase needed; simulation robustness does not demonstrate sim-to-real success or physical deployment skill. Runtime is unmeasured; no fixed cost or duration claim.
portfolioProposal.imitationExtension: If compute permits, use the verified LeRobot MuJoCo keyboard cube-picking tutorial to record demonstrations, train ACT and evaluate on held-out initial conditions. Keep demonstration count and training budget explicit. This is a separate scoped extension rather than mandatory VLA training.
